skill.name: extract
skill.description: Extract and consolidate reusable components, design tokens, and patterns into your design system. Identifies opportunities for systematic reuse and enriches your component library.
skill.summary: Identifies reusable UI components, tokens, and patterns, then helps consolidate them into a design system.
skill.author: pbakaus

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md line 71 warns against creating overly generic components, and no network reconnaissance behavior or prompt injection content was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Create components so generic they're useless

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 71 says not to create components that are too generic. This is design system guidance, not network discovery, scanning, or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Teams often duplicate UI components, tokens, and layout patterns across an application. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code find reusable patterns and consolidate them into a maintained design system.
actual_capabilities: Locates existing design system, component library, or shared UI directories.
Identifies repeated components, hard-coded values, inconsistent variants, and reusable layout patterns.
Creates extraction plans covering components, tokens, variants, naming, and migration paths.
Builds reusable components with sensible props, accessibility support, and usage documentation.
Defines design tokens with clear naming, hierarchy, and usage guidance.
Updates component library documentation, examples, and Storybook catalogs when present.
limitations: Requires access to the project source files that contain UI patterns.
Asks before creating a design system when none exists.
Cannot guarantee visual parity without project tests or human review.
Works best when the project already has clear naming and documentation conventions.

use_cases.title: Consolidate Duplicate Components
use_cases.description: Find repeated UI patterns and turn them into shared components with documented variants.

use_cases.title: Grow a Token System
use_cases.description: Convert repeated colors, spacing, typography, and shadows into named design tokens.

use_cases.title: Plan a UI Cleanup
use_cases.description: Review a feature area and create a practical migration plan for reusable patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Find Extraction Candidates
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of one feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the extract skill on {target}. Identify repeated components, hard-coded design values, and reusable layout patterns. Summarize what should be extracted first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Component Reuse
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the extract skill to create an extraction plan for {target}. Include proposed components, variants, prop names, token needs, and migration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Shared Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced implementation in an existing design system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the extract skill to implement the approved extraction plan for {target}. Match existing design system conventions, add accessibility support, and update documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate and Document Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup after reusable assets are created.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the extract skill to replace old implementations in {target} with shared components and tokens. Confirm visual parity, remove dead code, and update catalog examples.

output_examples.input: Review the checkout flow for reusable UI patterns.
output_examples.output: Findings include repeated summary cards, duplicate button variants, and hard-coded spacing. Recommended extraction starts with summary card and checkout action components.

output_examples.input: Extract design tokens from the settings pages.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose semantic spacing, surface, text, and focus tokens, then map existing settings page values to those names.

output_examples.input: Move repeated profile components into the component library.
output_examples.output: The result would include a migration plan, reusable component boundaries, variant guidance, documentation updates, and a checklist for replacing old usages.

best_practices: Start with patterns used three or more times or likely to be reused soon.
Match existing component, token, import, and documentation conventions.
Test visual and functional parity before deleting old implementations.
anti_patterns: Do not extract one-off UI that has no clear reuse value.
Do not create generic components without a clear product purpose.
Do not turn every hard-coded value into a token without semantic meaning.

faq.question: Does this skill create a design system from scratch?
faq.answer: It can help plan one, but it should ask before creating a new design system.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing component library?
faq.answer: Yes. It first locates existing shared UI structure and follows local conventions.

faq.question: What kinds of patterns does it extract?
faq.answer: It focuses on repeated components, design tokens, layout patterns, and inconsistent UI variants.

faq.question: Does it handle accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill directs reusable components to include ARIA, keyboard navigation, and focus management where relevant.

faq.question: Will it update documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add examples, guidelines, and Storybook or component catalog entries when those tools exist.

faq.question: How should I choose a target?
faq.answer: Choose a feature, component group, or application area with visible duplication or inconsistent UI patterns.
